{"self_assessment": "Impact: I laid the whole bottom line of the fish, the long lower outline from the nose to the tail turn. It is about half the body and what gives the fish its belly curve. I built it in a steady series of short builds. Before the push, tracing by eye showed the fall reaching 117 of the 119 standing dominoes, with both tail tips included.

Execution: I started the bottom stroke a hand's width short of the line it grows from, as the process requires, and kept the work moving. I inspected the nose join closely twice, once mid-build and once later. I confirmed the fall carries round the nose into the bottom line. I also identified the only two loose dominoes, which sit off the outline and won't show. I left them alone and kept everyone's hands off, so nothing got bumped in the final minutes.

Collaboration: Early on I proposed a clear split, with me on the whole bottom line and Maya on the tail fork. That avoided doubling up. I called out when I reached the tail turn so Maya could start her fork without building over mine. When I was about to overlap her lower-tip stretch, I stepped off and let her keep it. I thanked Tom for curving in the nose. I kept the manager updated whenever they checked in.

Leadership: I helped set the plan and the division of labour, and I made the call to stop touching the build once it was verified. I called for hands off so the result stayed safe until the push. I held myself to checking the joins rather than assuming they worked.

The fish was a team result. Priya laid the top and the start, Maya the tail, and Tom the nose curve. I see my share as the bottom line, the nose verification and the coordination.", "my_share_percent": 30}
